BoviSense AI

Cattle counting with computer vision at the edge.

The problem

Ranchers spend hours counting cattle manually, and human error makes herd tracking less reliable.

My contribution

End-to-end architecture: detection model, hardware integration, API, mobile app and end-to-end testing.

Result

Detection mAP of 0.87. Counting time dropped from ~2 hours manually to ~5 minutes per batch.

About me

Technical curiosity. Product thinking.

I care about software that solves a problem for someone. I work from interface to data, and especially enjoy projects that combine web development, AI and hardware.

I’m Rover, a Computer Systems Engineering graduate (Univalle, 2026). My final-year project, BoviSense, took me from computer vision on a Jetson to a Flutter app and a Node backend. It taught me that useful software connects product, data and infrastructure.

Before that, I built management systems, a credential vault and a sentiment analysis platform. The approach was always the same: understand the problem, narrow the scope and deliver something that works.

I’m looking for my first full-stack role on a team that builds products, reviews code and shares direct feedback. I’m available remotely or in Cochabamba.

Product first

I think about the person using the system before choosing the technology. The simplest solution is often the best.

AI that works in practice

Models that run in real conditions: edge computing, latency, hardware and messy data. A metric matters when it helps solve a problem.

Readable code

Clear names, small components and documentation so another developer can pick up the work without guessing.
